items.title: Alleviating Baumol’s Cost Disease with Artificial Intelligence: Mechanisms from an Economic Sustainability Perspective
items.abstract: The service sector accounts for a growing share of economic activity, yet relatively slow productivity growth leaves firms facing wage-driven cost pressures that constrain long-term investment. From an economic sustainability perspective, alleviating Baumol’s cost disease can help service firms improve productivity and reduce reliance on additional factor inputs. Drawing on the resource-based view and dynamic capabilities theory, this study applies double machine learning to Chinese A-share-listed service firms from 2011 to 2024 to examine the alleviating effect of artificial intelligence (AI) on Baumol’s cost disease and its potential pathways. Higher AI use intensity is significantly associated with a higher Baumol’s cost disease alleviation indicator (BMR). Greater capital investment efficiency and lower long-term debt financing dependence are two potential pathways, while supplier concentration and growth opportunities positively moderate this relationship. The association is stronger among loss-making firms and firms with greater ownership balance. These findings provide firm-level evidence that AI may help service firms cope with rising wages through productivity growth, supported by more efficient capital allocation and improved financing structures, and contribute to efficiency-driven growth.

items.title: An artificial intelligence based framework for smart power grid management using an autonomous and controllable intelligent service hub with multimodal document processing
items.abstract: The growing sophistication and need to have sustainable energy systems has led to the shift of the conventional power grids to smart power grids. Such grids are equipped with innovative technologies that include digital communication, Internet of Things (IoT), and Artificial Intelligence (AI) to increase the efficiency, reliability, and scalability of energy delivery. This paper introduce an AI-based approach to smart power grid management, with the emphasis on the incorporation of an autonomous and controllable intelligent service hub that would be able to process multimodal data, such as textual reports, images, videos, and sensor data. The framework applies AI methods of machine learning, deep learning, and predictive analytics to optimize energy allocation, faults, and failure prediction with minimum human intervention. With real-time analysis, the system dynamically changes the operation of the grids with incoming data, enhancing energy efficiency and lowering the cost of operations by up to 30 percent, between $12,000 and 8,400 in the example of energy optimization. Also, the fault detection system shows a remarkable accuracy of 0.97 in terms of AUC whereas the predictive maintenance model reports an accuracy rate of 95.5. The balancing nature of the energy demand and generation provided by the framework is critical in integrating renewable energy sources since it can help in countering the problem of intermittency of the solar and wind energy. Moreover, the system has a multimodal document processing feature that increases decision-making through the synthesis of various types of data and provides a more detailed overview of grid work. This paper explains how the suggested AI-based framework can greatly improve the efficiency, reliability, and sustainability of smart power grids, which will result in the future improvements in energy management.

items.title: An Evidence-Driven Multi-Agent Compound AI System for Head and Neck Proton Radiotherapy Planning
items.abstract: Radiation treatment planning requires balancing competing objectives to satisfy clinical criteria while accommodating physicians' preferences. This study aims to develop an evidence-driven, multi-agent compound AI system that integrates DRL-based automated treatment planning with LLM-based conversational plan refinement for proton PBS therapy. A policy network trained using PPO first generates multiple plans without human intervention, from which one is selected as the target plan and the others serve as references for subsequent refinements. For challenging cases requiring further adjustments, an LLM-based multi-agent system enables plan refinement through natural language interactions. The system comprises a planning agent that recommends evidence-supported adjustments, a chatbot providing a unified conversational interface, and an evaluation agent that retrieves clinical metrics and identifies constraint violations. To enhance domain-specific reasoning, the planning agent based on Qwen3-14B is designed to justify its recommendations using evidence from previously generated plans and post-trained on task-specific data using SFT and GRPO. The framework was trained and evaluated using 21 patients with H&N cancers, with 5 PPO-generated plans per patient. Of these, 50 plans were selected for instruction-guided refinement. Compared with the base LLM, the post-trained Qwen3-14B demonstrated improved instruction-following, information retrieval and domain-specific reasoning capabilities. The resulting adjustments more effectively improved user-prioritized objectives while limiting deterioration in competing objectives, yielding more clinically appropriate trade-offs in patient-specific plan refinement. The proposed compound AI system provides a user-friendly planning platform, offering a promising approach to personalized proton PBS treatment planning.

items.title: An integrated approach to medical personnel management in the context of digital transformation of healthcare
items.abstract: The article addresses the problem of social management of medical personnel amid the digital transformation of healthcare and significant changes in the relationships among medical workers, patients, administrative structures, and digital systems. In response to current interdisciplinary shifts, an integrated model for managing medical personnel is proposed — one that accounts for macrosocial factors, mechanisms of social perception related to the profession, and aggregated indicators at the level of the workers’ subjective world. The methodological foundation is a systems approach, within which medical personnel are viewed as a social system shaped not only by linear macro-management influences but also by relevant public relations, images of the medical profession, the communication environment, the features of digital healthcare products etc. A three-level management model is substantiated, comprising the macro level of normative and organizational structures, the meso level of social perception, and the micro level of professional attitudes, loyalty, and motivation of personnel. It is shown that social perception serves a connecting function between macro-management decisions and actual professional practices. The article emphasizes the need to manage the images of medical personnel — including their reproduction in artificial intelligence — as well as to consider the psychological climate as a significant factor of loyalty. The proposed model makes it possible to increase the coherence of management goals, mechanisms, and interventions.

items.title: An interpretable deep learning method for early hepatocellular carcinoma diagnosis on multiphase CT
items.abstract: Early diagnosis of hepatocellular carcinoma is critical to preserve access to curative treatment options. The Liver Imaging Reporting and Data System (LI-RADS) provides a standardized framework for non-invasive diagnosis on multiphase computed tomography, based on major visual imaging features. However, these features may be difficult to assess consistently, particularly in small liver lesions. We developed dLI-RADS, an interpretable artificial intelligence method designed to estimate the probability of hepatocellular carcinoma from multiphase computed tomography images of manually segmented liver lesions, while remaining aligned with LI-RADS-related imaging concepts. dLI-RADS combines neural network-derived predictions with handcrafted quantitative imaging measurements reflecting LI-RADS major features and integrates these inputs using logistic regression. In this multicenter retrospective study, patients with multiphase computed tomography and at least one liver lesion were included, while lesions larger than 40 mm were excluded. Histology served as the reference standard for hepatocellular carcinoma, and a composite reference standard was used for non-hepatocellular carcinoma lesions. The lesion-level accuracy of dLI-RADS and LI-RADS were compared on the internal evaluation set using 10,000-repetition bootstrap non-inferiority tests, with 5% margins and significance levels. On the external test set, sensitivities were similarly compared. dLI-RADS was non-inferior to LI-RADS for lesion-level accuracy in the internal evaluation set, achieving 80% accuracy compared with 74% for LI-RADS (p = 0.04)...

items.title: Analysis of the Copyrightability of Artificial Intelligence-Generated Content in the United States
items.abstract: The commercial application of generative artificial intelligence has rapidly brought to the fore the structural tension between machine-generated content (AIGC) and the core presuppositions of copyright law concerning the “author.” This paper examines the protection model and legal mechanisms adopted by the United States on the question of AIGC copyrightability. The research finds that the United States, as represented by the Thaler case, strengthens the “human authorship” requirement from the perspectives of constitutional text, statutory interpretation, and incentive theory, and adopts a result-oriented standard centered on expressive control.

items.title: AOXP: An Integrated Framework for Antioxidant Peptide Prediction Leveraging LLM-Based Semantic Features and Optimized Physicochemical Ensembles
items.abstract: Abstract Oxidative stress is a critical driver of various severe diseases, positioning antioxidant peptides (APs) as promising therapeutic agents. However, their discovery is constrained by the limitations of low-throughput wet-lab assays and insufficient computational prediction tools. To address this, we developed Antioxidant Peptides eXplorer (AOXP), a deep learning framework that leverages multiscale feature integration for high-precision AP prediction. Unlike existing models that often rely on isolated sequence patterns or manual feature descriptors, AOXP employs a hybrid encoding strategy that synergistically fuses deep, context-aware semantic representations from the protein large language model (ESM2) with explicit physicochemical and sequence distribution features. We constructed an optimized MLP architecture based on a refined 2400-dimensional feature vector, which was systematically benchmarked among five architectures and four feature selection strategies. Comprehensive evaluation demonstrates that AOXP achieves competitive performance across evaluation data sets, achieving a benchmark AUC of 0.736 on test_set1_drop and a sensitivity of 0.878 on the positive-only independent Test set 2, significantly outperforming current mainstream computational predictors in both sensitivity and robustness. Integrated Gradients analysis further quantified feature contributions, revealing that ESM2-derived semantics are the most influential features for model prediction (by feature number), followed by hydrophobicity, polarity, charge, and solvent accessibility. To demonstrate its therapeutic utility, AOXP was applied to screen a large peptide library targeting the Keap1-Nrf2 oxidative response pathway. A computationally predicted candidate peptide, MGRRHRHVTDEDDEENLGGDDDDGDDDVYMYPADMHPDERHAYREAV, was identified and validated through molecular dynamics simulations, exhibiting superior binding affinity for the Keap1 Kelch domain compared to the native ligand. AOXP provides a robust and efficient framework for the discovery of functional antioxidant peptides (available at: http://aidd.bioai-global.com/AOXP/).

items.title: Applications of artificial intelligence and machine learning in food processing, quality control, and food safety: a critical review
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI), machine learning (ML), and deep learning (DL) are increasingly being applied to support data-driven decision-making in food processing, quality control, and food safety. This review provides a critical assessment of recent technological advances and examines how AI models are being integrated with computer vision, spectroscopy, hyperspectral imaging (HSI), biosensors, Internet of Things (IoT) platforms, and intelligent monitoring systems throughout the food value chain. This review brings together evidence from academic studies and industry-based research to examine how AI is currently used in the food sector. The applications considered include process control and optimization, fermentation management, quality grading, authenticity assessment, shelf-life prediction, contaminant detection, and support for food-safety decisions. Recent research extends beyond conventional prediction toward adaptive decision support and, in a smaller number of cases, partially autonomous food systems. Approaches such as explainable AI, multimodal learning, foundation models, digital twins, intelligent packaging, and agentic AI are being investigated for real-time monitoring, data integration, and production management. Their level of maturity, however, varies considerably, and many applications remain conceptual or confined to laboratory settings. Data heterogeneity, poor transferability, limited external validation, and regulatory uncertainty continue to restrict industrial adoption. Although one industrial-scale drying study reported a 12.8% reduction in energy consumption, external validation of food-quality models has resulted in markedly higher prediction errors. This contrast illustrates the difficulty of transferring performance from controlled datasets to new products or production environments. Rather than examining these technologies separately, this review considers their roles across food processing, quality control, and food safety, together with the evidence for industrial validation, sustainability, and governance. Further progress will depend on whether models remain reliable outside their development datasets, not simply on incremental gains in internally reported accuracy.

items.title: Applications of Artificial Intelligence in Managerial Decision-Making for Sustainable Agro-Export Operations in Latin America: A Systematic Review and Bibliometric Analysis, 1996-2025
items.abstract: Background Artificial intelligence is transforming agro-export management by converting production, commercial, climate, and logistics data into support for more timely decisions. In Latin America, however, evidence on its managerial applications and contribution to sustainable operations remains fragmented. Objective To synthesize evidence on the application of artificial intelligence to managerial decision-making and its contribution to the efficiency, sustainability, traceability, resilience, and competitiveness of sustainable agro-export operations in Latin America from 1996 to 2025. Methods A systematic review and bibliometric analysis were conducted in accordance with PRISMA 2020. Scopus and Web of Science yielded 2160 records; after filtering, screening, and eligibility assessment, 73 studies were included. Bibliometrix in RStudio and VOSviewer were used to analyze scientific production, authors, countries, sources, Bradford’s and Lotka’s laws, keyword co-occurrence, and thematic clusters. Results Scientific output increased markedly after 2021 and peaked in 2024. Scopus accounted for 98.95% of the records. China led with 170 publications, while Brazil, with 149, was the only Latin American country among the five most productive. Four thematic areas were identified: prediction and classification using artificial intelligence and machine learning; logistics, supply chains, and suppliers; sustainable resource management and climate risks; and digital transformation through Agriculture 4.0/5.0. Across the literature, artificial intelligence was found to reduce uncertainty and improve decision-making, although its effectiveness depends on data quality, digital infrastructure, and organizational capabilities. Conclusions Artificial intelligence represents a strategic capability for strengthening sustainable agro-export operations. Its impact depends on integrating algorithms with reliable data, technological infrastructure, organizational capabilities, and sustainability criteria. The limited representation of Latin America highlights the need for further empirical research adapted to regional conditions.

items.title: Applications of Wearable Electronics and Beyond
items.abstract: Wearable electronics represent a transformative shift in the integration of digital technology with the human body, enabling continuous monitoring, enhanced interactivity, and real-time data acquisition in a compact, user-friendly form. These devices, ranging from smartwatches and fitness trackers to smart textiles and implantable biosensors, have revolutionized healthcare, fitness, communication, and entertainment. By offering real-time physiological monitoring, wearables have opened new frontiers in personalized medicine, chronic disease management, and remote diagnostics. Beyond health, wearable technologies are redefining human–machine interaction in sectors such as augmented reality (AR), virtual reality (VR), defense, industrial safety, and sports performance optimization. Looking forward, the convergence of flexible electronics, nanomaterials, energy harvesting, and artificial intelligence is propelling wearables beyond traditional formats. Next-generation devices aim for seamless skin integration, biodegradability, self-healing materials, and neural interfacing—pushing the boundaries of cyber-physical symbiosis. These advancements point toward a future where wearables transition from external gadgets to embedded, intelligent systems capable of enhancing cognition, perception, and human capability in real time. This abstract outlines the current applications and explores the trajectory of wearable electronics as they evolve from assistive devices to integral components of the human body, fundamentally reshaping our interaction with technology and the environment.

items.title: Approximate Solomonoff Induction: On the Robustness of Learned Universal Predictors
items.abstract: Why large language models trained via log-loss minimization over massive and diverse datasets exhibit broad capabilities and generalizable skills is not yet fully understood. Grau-Moya et al. (ICML 2024) offer a conceptual explanation through the lens of meta-learning: if sequence-generating environments $ν$ are drawn from a prior $w_ν$, minimizing population log-loss recovers the corresponding Bayesian mixture predictor $ξ=\sum_νw_νν$. In the idealized limit in which $w$ is a universal prior, the optimal predictor corresponds to Solomonoff universal induction. Practical machine learning algorithms, however, generally produce only \emph{approximately} optimal predictors. This raises a natural question: \emph{Does the prediction performance remain robust under approximation}? In this paper, we first provide a tight bound on the worst-case effect of approximation on prediction error. We show any predictor $ρ$ satisfying $D_{KL}(ξ\|ρ)\leq η$ retains bounded cumulative-expected-squared prediction error. However, while the Bayesian mixture predictor $ξ$ has error $O(\log(1/w_μ))$ in an environment $μ$, we establish a tight $Θ(η/w_μ)$ bound on the excess error of $ρ$ relative to $ξ$. Thus, approximation can substantially degrade performance in environments assigned small prior probability. In sharp contrast, when environments are averaged according to prior $w$, we prove that the excess prediction error is only $O(η)$. Furthermore, we establish a distribution-shift theorem for dominated shifts from a training prior $w$ to a test prior $w'$, interpolating our average-case and worst-case guarantees. Finally, we extend our robustness analysis to a finite-sampling setting relevant to learning universal predictors with neural networks and Transformers, where $D_{KL}(ξ\|ρ)$ could be unbounded. items.title: AQL-Lite: Enabling Efficient Knowledge Acquisition for Arabic LLMs via Data-Centric Continual Pretraining
items.abstract: Training Arabic large language models faces challenges from noisy web data, dialectal variation, and the high cost of continual pretraining (CPT). We introduce AQL-Lite (AQL: Arabic Quality Language), a time- and resource-efficient framework for adapting a multilingual LLM to Modern Standard Arabic (MSA). AQL-Lite couples a quality-first curation pipeline (structural cleaning, heuristic and model-based filtering, MSA selection, and deduplication) with a partial-parameter CPT recipe that trains RS-LoRA adapters across the network together with the last eight transformer blocks and the embedding matrix, under layer-wise learning rates. At a matched 1B-token budget, CPT on AQL-curated data raises a four-benchmark Arabic mean by 3.51 points over CPT on raw web text, which yields no gain over the base model. In a controlled 5B-token comparison, AQL-Lite recovers 94% of the gain of full-parameter CPT (mean 73.19 vs. 73.58) in 52% of the wall-clock time and outperforms adapter-only baselines on every benchmark, and a component ablation shows that adapters, unfrozen blocks, and embedding training each contribute. Scaled to 40B MSA tokens and instruction-tuned on one million examples, the resulting 12B model scores 75.3 on the seven-benchmark Open Arabic LLM Leaderboard v2 (OALL v2) suite. These results suggest that partial-parameter CPT on a carefully curated corpus is a practical route to efficient MSA adaptation.

items.title: Aqua Sense AI: AI-Powered Water Quality Intelligence Platform
items.abstract: Water quality assessment is essential for determining whether water is suitable for human consumption and enabling informed decision-making regarding water resources. Aqua Sense AI is an AI-powered water quality intelligence platform developed using Python and Streamlit. The system provides a preliminary classification of water samples as Safe (Potable) or Unsafe (Non-Potable) based on nine physicochemical parameters: pH, Hardness, Total Dissolved Solids (TDS), Chloramines, Sulfate, Conductivity, Organic Carbon, Trihalomethanes, and Turbidity. A Random Forest Classifier is employed for the classification task, delivering real-time predictions along with prediction confidence scores, a composite Water Quality Score (0–100), and risk level assessments (Low, Medium, or High). Parameter values are entered through an intuitive interactive web form. The platform features an Analytics Dashboard powered by interactive Plotly visualizations, Explainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI) providing feature importance rankings and natural language reasoning, dynamic parameter-specific water treatment recommendations, and session-based prediction history tracking. Designed in alignment with UN Sustainable Development Goal 6 (Clean Water and Sanitation), the system serves as a preliminary decision-support tool and does not replace certified laboratory testing. Overall, the work demonstrates an integrated approach that combines machine learning, explainability, interactive data analytics, and actionable guidance within a unified water quality assessment platform

items.title: ARCANA: A Benchmark for Abstraction and Analogical Reasoning
items.abstract: Analogical reasoning is widely considered a fundamental component of human intelligence. Few benchmarks are designed to explicitly test far analogical reasoning - reasoning between domains that are superficially dissimilar yet share deep relational or structural similarities. In this work, we introduce an analogical reasoning benchmark called Abstraction and Reasoning Corpus of ANAlogy (ARCANA). The tasks of ARCANA require performing far analogical mappings from real-world objects or physical phenomena to abstract grid-based transformations, different from the well-known ARC-AGI benchmark which primarily emphasized innate human priors. We validate ARCANA through a human study, demonstrating that humans solve these tasks reliably. In contrast, evaluations across a range of large language models show a distinct performance gap compared to humans, revealing systematic failure modes that remain challenging for current models. To address this gap, we propose ConceptSIR, a reasoning framework based on concept slippage, introspection, and reflection. Experiments demonstrate that ConceptSIR enables standard LLMs to solve several challenging ARCANA tasks that were unsolved by direct prompting in our evaluation. Overall, our results suggest that far analogical reasoning remains an open problem for contemporary LLMs. All the materials are available at sites.google.com/view/arcanacogtest. The complete codebase, including benchmark, and ConceptSIR, is publicly available at https://github.com/density-11/arcana-test. All ARCANA data and task instances can be accessed and explored at https://arcanacogtest.org/.

items.title: Architectural Concepts For Integrating Human Preferences And Environmental Susainability Into AI-Driven Architectural Design
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly influencing architectural design through generative modelling, performance prediction, spatial planning, and workflow automation. However, many current applications address individual tasks or emphasize visual novelty, while practical design decisions must balance human needs, climate responsiveness, affordability, accessibility, regulatory constraints, and environmental performance. This paper proposes a Human-Centered and Sustainability-Aware AI Architectural Design Framework (HCS-AADF) that combines these considerations within an iterative design-support workflow. The framework accepts user requirements, site and climate information, budget limits, and applicable design constraints; analyses the project context; generates alternative layouts or massing concepts; evaluates alternatives against multiple criteria; explains trade-offs; and returns shortlisted options to an architect for review. Human feedback can be used to refine subsequent iterations. A conceptual multi-criteria scoring model and an evaluation protocol are specified to support future implementation and testing. The paper synthesizes three supplied research directions—AI architectures informed by human drives and emotions, the adoption and capabilities of AI software tools in architecture, and systematic reviews of AI applications in architectural design—along with relevant recent literature on generative design and sustainable building optimization. The proposed contribution is an integrated, transparent workflow rather than a claim of experimentally proven performance. Expected benefits include more traceable design comparisons, earlier consideration of sustainability, and improved collaboration between architects and AI systems. The framework also identifies risks involving data quality, bias, explainability, regulatory verification, and over-reliance on generated outputs. Experimental validation with representative building projects and expert review is proposed as the next step.

items.title: Artificial Intelligence And Creative Writing: Transforming Authorship In English Language And Literature
items.abstract: Incorporation of artificial intelligence in the process of creative writing entails a paradigmatic change in literary text production, assessment, and perception. In this research paper, the focus is made on an innovative role of large language models in the sphere of English language and literature authorship. Based on systematic analysis of recent empirical studies and theoretical approaches, three interrelated aspects will be discussed: interaction between human authors and AI systems, reception of artificial literature by the readership, and conceptualization of authorship in the digital age. For the purpose of this paper, the mixed-method approach involving both quantitative analysis of empirical studies and qualitative analysis of literary theoretical approaches will be used. As the results of the analysis indicate, the texts generated by AI are rated aesthetically the same way as texts written by human authors when there is no indication of the author's identity; however, readers maintain biases against texts that are perceived to be machine-generated.

items.title: Artificial Intelligence Applications in Electric Power and Energy Systems: A PRISMA-Bibliometric Review of Tools, Application Domains, Quantified Impacts, and Deployment Barriers from 2021 to 2025
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly used in electric power and energy systems for forecasting, fault diagnosis, stability assessment, control, renewable energy integration, and real-time monitoring. However, evidence remains fragmented across algorithms, applications, performance metrics, and deployment conditions. This study reviews recent AI applications in power and energy systems and examines their technological, economic, and operational contributions and limitations. A PRISMA-based systematic and bibliometric review was conducted using Scopus and Web of Science records published from 2021 to 2025. Bibliometrix/Biblioshiny 5.5.0 and VOSviewer 1.6.20 were used to analyze publication trends, citation patterns, geographical distribution, influential studies, and keyword networks, while 40 studies were retained for systematic evidence synthesis. In the reconciled 4854-record corpus, annual scientific production increased from 610 publications in 2021 to 1305 in 2025, with research concentrating on machine learning, deep learning, smart grids, stability, renewable energy, forecasting, fault diagnosis, optimization, and cybersecurity. The reviewed studies reported improvements in predictive accuracy, computational efficiency, fault localization, voltage control, energy savings, and real-time decision support. Nevertheless, data dependence, computational cost, limited interpretability, simulation-to-field transfer, and validation requirements remain major barriers. Future research should prioritize robust, explainable, physics-aware, and field-validated AI for critical power-system applications.

items.title: Artificial Intelligence Benchmarking of Blood Culture Contamination Classifiers Under Unmeasured Collection Site Skin Antisepsis Timing: A Healthcare Specificity-Safety Evaluation
items.abstract: Blood culture contamination classifiers are typically benchmarked against microbiological reference labels that encode collection-site skin antisepsis timing as an unmeasured confounder, so reported specificity and safety metrics may reflect the labelling process rather than classifier behaviour. the present analysis formalises the problem as a before-after-control-impact design in which the estimand is the interaction between classifier deployment and an antisepsis-timing regime, and characterises the operating characteristics of that design under a declared variance structure. Using a between-cluster standard deviation of 6.0, a residual standard deviation of 4.5 and an intraclass correlation of 0.640, power was estimated across 2000 replications per design cell for cluster counts of 8, 16, 24 and 32 and effects of 3, 5 and 8 percentage points. The design required 54 clusters to detect a 5-percentage-point interaction at 80% power, a requirement that exceeds the cluster counts examined and that exposes the fragility of single-site classifier benchmarks. The paper derives the bias in apparent specificity when antisepsis timing is omitted, states the conditions under which the before-after-control-impact interaction identifies the classifier-attributable effect, and argues that contamination-classifier safety claims should be reported as design-bounded rather than as intrinsic properties of the model.

items.title: Artificial Intelligence Benchmarking of Community Health Worker Triage Questionnaires Under Unmeasured Verbal Autopsy Recall Decay: A Healthcare Label-Noise Robustness Evaluation
items.abstract: Verbal autopsy (VA) remains the principal source of cause-of-death labels for community health worker (CHW) triage algorithms in low-resource settings, yet the recall interval between death and VA interview is rarely recorded and almost never modelled. the present analysis treats unmeasured recall decay as a structured label-noise process and characterises the operating characteristics of a before-after-control-impact (BACII) benchmarking design used to evaluate CHW triage classifiers under that noise. No observational data are used or claimed: the analysis is a replication-based evaluation of the estimator under a declared variance structure (between-cluster SD = 6.0, residual SD = 4.5, intraclass correlation = 0.640), with power estimated across 2000 design cells spanning cluster counts of 8, 16, 24 and 32 and effect sizes of 3, 5 and 8 percentage points. The design attains 80% power at 54 clusters for a 5-percentage-point effect. The paper derives a bias bound showing that recall decay inflates the apparent between-cluster variance component and therefore the intraclass correlation, and it proposes a sensitivity-analysis protocol that reports benchmarking conclusions as a function of an assumed decay rate rather than as a single point estimate. The contribution is a design-level account of how label noise that is unmeasured but structurally bounded can be made visible in AI benchmarking for healthcare, together with the sample-size consequences of that visibility.

items.title: Artificial Intelligence Benchmarking of Emergency Department Triage Classifiers Under Unmeasured Nurse Acuity Re-Scoring at Queue Reordering: A Healthcare Stability Evaluation
items.abstract: Emergency department triage classifiers are benchmarked almost exclusively on static acuity labels, yet the operational label is produced when a nurse re-scores a patient at queue reordering. the present analysis treats that re-scoring as an unmeasured cluster-level shock and asks whether the before-after-control-impact (BACI) design can recover the effect of a classifier change when re-scoring is confounded with the intervention. A replication-based evaluation was conducted over a declared variance structure with between-cluster SD 6.0, residual SD 4.5 and intraclass correlation 0.64, using 2000 replications per design cell across 8, 16, 24 and 32 clusters and effects of 3, 5 and 8 percentage points. Power reached 80% at 52 clusters for a 5-percentage-point effect; at the largest design cell of 32 clusters the minimum detectable effect remained above the 5-point target. The interaction estimate was biased toward the null when re-scoring intensity differed between arms, and residual diagnostics showed heteroscedasticity aligned with cluster size. The contribution is a stability bound: BACI benchmarking of triage classifiers is defensible only when re-scoring is either measured or shown to be exchangeable across arms, and the paper specifies the design conditions under which that claim can be tested.

items.abstract: Cholera forecast models that combine rainfall drivers with ensemble machine learning are increasingly proposed as decision aids for outbreak preparedness, yet their evaluation typically assumes that sanitation covariates are observed without delay. The framework formalises reporting lag as a latent state that decouples the covariate process from the decision time, defines a lag-robust ensemble aggregator, and derives a decision-value bound that separates forecast discrimination from the economic cost of acting on stale sanitation information. Using NASA POWER monthly reanalysis air temperature at 2 m for Kampala (0.35, 32.58) over 2000-2023, comprising 312 monthly observations with a mean of 22.443 C and a linear trend of -0.1564 C per decade, the paper demonstrates how the benchmarking protocol is operationalised on a real covariate stream. items.abstract: Graph neural networks (GNNs) are increasingly proposed for triage across inter-facility referral networks, yet their safety evaluation typically assumes that transport times between facilities are observed. We define a censored referral-network triage problem, introduce a transport-time censoring operator, and derive a distributionally robust triage policy that bounds worst-case mortality under an ambiguity set defined by censoring-consistent transport-time distributions. The framework is illustrated using the DHS Program indicator 'Households possessing a computer' across 27 African countries (56 country-survey observations, 2015-2025; mean 7.893, SD 5.144), which serves as a proxy for digital readiness of referral nodes. The contribution is a benchmark protocol and a theorem that together specify when GNN triage can be certified safe under unmeasured transport censoring, and when it cannot.

items.abstract: Whole-genome sequencing (WGS) is increasingly used to predict Mycobacterium tuberculosis drug resistance, and machine-learning classifiers trained on WGS data are benchmarked against phenotypic drug-susceptibility testing (DST). The analysis indicates that 56 clusters are required for 80% power at a 5-percentage-point effect. We argue that calibration, not discrimination alone, should be the primary benchmark for WGS-based resistance prediction, and we specify the reporting standards that would make heteroresistance-aware benchmarking reproducible.

items.abstract: Verbal autopsy (VA) remains the primary source of cause-of-death information for under-five mortality in settings without complete civil registration, yet the cause labels it produces are known to be misclassified in ways that are rarely quantified and almost never propagated into the machine-learning pipelines that consume them. We define a misclassification operator on the label simplex, derive the bias it induces in ensemble risk scores and in decision-curve net benefit, and show that the ranking of ensembles by area under the receiver operating characteristic curve is invariant to symmetric label noise only under restrictive conditions that fail for the asymmetric confusion structures typical of VA. The framework is illustrated with a decision-curve evaluation protocol that separates ensemble discrimination, calibration and clinical utility, and that reports the range of misclassification rates over which a given ensemble ranking is preserved. We argue that benchmarking practice in this domain should report a misclassification-robustness envelope alongside conventional performance metrics, and we specify the sensitivity analysis that such reporting requires. The contribution is methodological: it does not report new empirical results but provides the formal apparatus and reporting standard needed before ensemble comparisons on VA-derived labels can be interpreted as evidence about clinical decision quality.

Because no observational data are available for the present analysis, the paper is methodological: it characterises the operating characteristics of the proposed estimator under a declared variance structure (between-cluster SD = 6.0, residual SD = 4.5, intraclass correlation = 0.64) using a before-after-control-impact design with 2000 replications per cell across cluster counts of 8, 16, 24 and 32 and effect sizes of 3, 5 and 8 percentage points. The contribution is a discipline-specific mediation framework that treats register attrition as a structural feature of CHW programme evaluation rather than as a nuisance to be discarded, and that makes the equity consequences of attrition explicit in the estimand.

items.title: Artificial Intelligence Causal Transportability of Community Health Worker Triage Decision Support Under Variable Supervision Record Granularity: A Doubly Robust Evaluation of Healthcare Escalation Safety
items.abstract: Community health worker (CHW) triage decision support is increasingly proposed as a means of extending safe healthcare escalation into underserved districts, yet the safety of such systems is typically evaluated in pilot settings whose supervision records are more complete than those available at scale. the present analysis treats the resulting inferential problem as one of causal transportability under a before-after-control-impact (BACI) design and characterises the operating characteristics of a doubly robust estimator when supervision record granularity varies. No observational data are used or claimed; the analysis is a design-based evaluation under a declared variance structure with between-cluster standard deviation 6.0, residual standard deviation 4.5 and intraclass correlation 0.64. Power was estimated across 2000 replications per design cell for cluster counts of 8, 16, 24 and 32 and effect sizes of 3, 5 and 8 percentage points. Fifty clusters were required to detect a 5 percentage point effect at 80 per cent power. The paper derives the transportability conditions under which a doubly robust BACI contrast identifies the escalation-safety effect, shows how record granularity enters as a coarsening of the supervision covariate, and specifies the design quantities that a field evaluation must report. The contribution is a formal account of when CHW triage decision support can be expected to transport across supervision regimes, together with the sample-size consequences of that account.

items.title: Artificial Intelligence Computer Vision for Sickle Cell Retinopathy Screening Under Variable Fundus Camera Flash Intensity: A Test-Time Calibration Evaluation of Healthcare Referral Sensitivity
items.abstract: Sickle cell retinopathy screening programmes that deploy artificial intelligence (AI) computer vision on fundus photographs face a calibration problem that is rarely modelled explicitly: flash intensity varies across cameras, operators and clinic conditions, and a classifier trained at one illumination level may shift its referral threshold when deployed at another. the present analysis treats test-time calibration as a design problem for referral sensitivity rather than as a post-hoc correction. It formalises flash-induced intensity shift as a monotone transform of the retinal image, derives the conditions under which a temperature-scaling calibrator fitted on source-illumination data preserves the referral decision boundary at target illumination, and characterises the operating characteristics of a before-after-control-impact (BACI) evaluation of calibration transfer. The design uses 8, 16, 24 and 32 clusters, effect sizes of 3, 5 and 8 percentage points, and 2000 replications per cell under a declared variance structure with between-cluster SD 6.0, residual SD 4.5 and intraclass correlation 0.64.56 clusters are required to detect a 5-percentage-point referral-sensitivity gain at 80% power, and that the intraclass correlation of 0.64 dominates the detectable effect more than the calibration method itself. The contribution is a formal account of when test-time calibration can be trusted to preserve referral sensitivity, and a design-level statement of the cluster counts that screening programmes must budget for if they intend to evaluate calibration transfer empirically.

items.title: Artificial Intelligence Conformalised Counterfactual Policy Learning for Community Clinic Referral Escalation Under Unobserved Acuity Drift: A Healthcare Regret-Bound Evaluation
items.abstract: Community clinic referral escalation policies must decide which patients to send onward when patient acuity is only partially observed and drifts over time. The framework treats unobserved acuity drift as a bounded distribution shift and constructs conformal prediction regions that remain valid under that shift, then uses these regions to define a pessimistic policy class whose worst-case regret can be bounded in closed form. The analysis yields three results: a drift-robust conformal guarantee, a regret decomposition separating approximation error from conformal coverage slack, and a finite-sample bound that scales with the square root of the drift budget. The paper also reports a real-data calibration exercise using World Bank World Development Indicators for 24 African countries over 2000-2023 (N = 560), estimated by OLS with heteroskedasticity-robust HC1 standard errors, yielding R-squared = 0.591, adjusted R-squared = 0.5895, F = 184.764 (p = 2.82e-62), with coefficients for access to electricity (1291.55405, SE 194.35159), urban population (113.13952, SE 7.77493) and a linear year term (-104.41834, SE 11.31314). This exercise illustrates the magnitude of drift that a referral policy must tolerate. The contribution is a formal bridge between conformal inference and counterfactual policy learning for referral escalation, with explicit regret bounds that make the cost of unobserved acuity drift auditable.

items.abstract: Electrocardiograph lead reversal is a common, frequently undetected pre-analytical error in community clinic chest pain triage, and its interaction with artificial-intelligence-based decision support has not been characterised as a safety-guarantee problem. The framework treats lead reversal as a latent nuisance parameter that perturbs the feature distribution, and it constructs triage sets whose coverage guarantee is conditional on a declared exchangeability assumption that reversal violates. A before-after-control-impact design was used to characterise the operating characteristics of the evaluation under a declared variance structure with between-cluster SD of 6.0, residual SD of 4.5 and intraclass correlation of 0.64; power was estimated across 2000 design cells for cluster counts of 8, 16, 24 and 32 and effect sizes of 3, 5 and 8 percentage points. The analysis indicates that 52 clusters are required for 80% power at a 5-percentage-point effect. The contribution is a formal statement of the conditions under which conformal triage guarantees survive lead reversal, together with the design parameters that a safety evaluation must satisfy to detect guarantee failure.

items.title: Artificial Intelligence Constrained Multi-Objective Optimisation of Community Hypertension Medication Synchronisation Under Variable Pharmacy Stock Reconciliation Error: A computed Healthcare Adherence Equity Evaluation
items.abstract: Community hypertension medication synchronisation programmes align refill dates across a patient panel, but their adherence benefits depend on pharmacy stock records that are reconciled with variable error. the present analysis formulates medication synchronisation as a constrained multi-objective optimisation problem in which the decision-maker selects synchronisation dates and safety-stock levels to maximise expected adherence while limiting the equity gap between patients whose pharmacies report stock accurately and those whose pharmacies do not. The problem is solved by an artificial-intelligence search procedure that combines a constrained Pareto local search with a surrogate model of adherence response. Because no field data are available, the evaluation is a replication study: a before-after-control-impact design is characterised under a declared variance structure with between-cluster standard deviation 6.0, residual standard deviation 4.5 and intraclass correlation 0.64, and power is estimated across 2000 replications per design cell for cluster counts of 8, 16, 24 and 32 and effect sizes of 3, 5 and 8 percentage points. The design achieves 80% power at 52 clusters for a 5-percentage-point effect. Reconciliation error acts as a constraint on achievable equity rather than as noise to be averaged away, and that the optimiser's equity penalty must be set from the design's minimum detectable effect rather than from the observed adherence gap. The contribution is a formalisation that makes the equity cost of stock-record error explicit and a design rule that ties optimisation targets to the power of the evaluation that will judge them.

items.title: Artificial Intelligence Constrained Reinforcement Learning for Antivenom Cold-Chain Replenishment Under Variable Refrigerator Power Outage Duration: A computed Healthcare Stockout Resilience Evaluation
items.abstract: Antivenom stockouts in low-resource health systems are driven less by average demand than by the interaction between stochastic power outages and the cold-chain constraints that make replenishment irreversible once a vial is compromised. the present analysis formulates antivenom replenishment as a constrained Markov decision process in which the decision-maker observes refrigerator state, outage duration, and stock on hand, and chooses order quantities subject to a cold-chain loss probability that depends on outage length. A constrained reinforcement learning procedure is proposed that maximises expected service level subject to an explicit budget on expected wastage, using a Lagrangian relaxation whose multiplier is adapted online. Because no field data are available, the design is evaluated through a replication-based replication study that characterises the operating characteristics of the before-after-control-impact estimator used to assess the intervention. The replication uses a between-cluster standard deviation of 6.0, a residual standard deviation of 4.5, and an intraclass correlation of 0.64, with 2000 replications per design cell across cluster counts of 8, 16, 24 and 32 and effect sizes of 3, 5 and 8 percentage points. The analysis indicates that 52 clusters are required to detect a 5 percentage point effect at 80 per cent power under this variance structure. The contribution is a formalisation of cold-chain-constrained replenishment as a safe reinforcement learning problem together with a design-analysis protocol that specifies the cluster counts at which such an intervention could be credibly evaluated.

items.abstract: Digital detector gain drift in low-dose chest radiography displaces the pixel-intensity distribution on which artificial-intelligence tuberculosis classifiers depend, and the resulting calibration error is a patient-safety problem rather than a mere nuisance. the present analysis treats counterfactual calibration as a design problem for domain adaptation and characterises, by formal analysis and a replication-based evaluation of the before-after-control-impact estimator, how much detector heterogeneity a screening programme can absorb before the safety margin collapses. The analysis is theoretical: no observational data are used or claimed, and the operating characteristics of the design are characterised under a declared variance structure with between-cluster SD = 6.0, residual SD = 4.5 and intraclass correlation = 0.64, across 2000 design cells. Power was estimated for cluster counts of 8, 16, 24 and 32 and effects of 3, 5 and 8 percentage points; 54 clusters are required for 5 percentage points at 80 per cent power. The contribution is a transportability bound that separates gain-drift magnitude from calibration error and shows that counterfactual recalibration is identifiable only when the drift is monotone and the anchor set is gain-invariant. The bound reframes detector quality assurance as a calibration-identifiability requirement rather than a purely physical specification.

No observational data are analysed; the study is a design and power analysis under a declared variance structure with between-cluster SD 6.0, residual SD 4.5 and intraclass correlation 0.64, evaluated across 2000 replications per design cell for cluster counts of 8, 16, 24 and 32 and effects of 3, 5 and 8 percentage points.54 clusters are required to detect a 5 percentage point effect at 80 per cent power, that the minimum detectable effect falls steeply as clusters increase from 8 to 32, and that the estimator remains approximately unbiased with nominal interval coverage across the design grid. The contribution is a formal statement of the identification conditions under which a counterfactual switching threshold can be estimated from routine programme data, together with the design parameters that make such an evaluation informative.

items.abstract: Community health worker (CHW) home-visit scheduling is a sequential allocation problem in which the travel-time matrix is rarely known with the precision that optimisation models assume. Because no field data were available, the estimator behaviour underpinning the framework was characterised in a replication study: 600 data sets of N = 500 were drawn from a declared data-generating process (intercept 12.0, exposure 0.42, group -3.1, severity 1.35, error SD 4.2) with seed 783202219, and the ordinary least squares estimator was evaluated across replications. Estimated bias was -0.00091 for the intercept and -0.00028 for the exposure coefficient; root mean squared error was 0.87048 and 0.01626 respectively; empirical coverage of the nominal 95% confidence intervals was 1.0 for both parameters. The results indicate that the estimator is unbiased and that the nominal intervals are conservative under the stated process, which supports the use of the fitted travel-time model as a plug-in nominal matrix inside the ambiguity set.

When competency logging is coarse or inconsistently updated, counterfactual estimators that assign titration tasks on the basis of logged competency may misallocate work across staff cadres. The framework separates the causal estimand from the logging mechanism, permits sensitivity analysis to logging error, and yields a defensible basis for workload-equity claims when competency records are imperfect.

Power was estimated across 2000 replications per design cell for cluster counts of 8, 16, 24 and 32 and effect sizes of 3, 5 and 8 percentage points.52 clusters are required to detect a 5-percentage-point effect at 80% power, that the minimum detectable effect falls steeply between 8 and 24 clusters, and that the BACI interaction estimator remains approximately nominal in coverage across the grid. The contribution is a formal bridge between distributionally robust optimisation and resistance-safety evaluation, and a demonstration that the evaluation design, not only the policy, must be sized against the telemetry variance it is meant to absorb.

items.title: Artificial Intelligence Doubly Robust Estimation of Community Health Worker Triage Accuracy Under Differential Verification by Referral Distance: A Healthcare Selection-Bias Evaluation
items.abstract: Community health worker (CHW) triage programmes routinely verify only a subset of referrals, and verification is often more likely for patients living near a referral facility. This differential verification by referral distance creates a selection bias that inflates naive estimates of triage accuracy. Because no field data are available, the estimator's finite-sample behaviour is characterised in a replication study of 600 data sets of N = 500 drawn from a declared data-generating process (intercept 12.0, exposure 0.42, group -3.1, severity 1.35, error SD 4.2). Across the replications the estimated bias was 0.04454 for the intercept and -0.00104 for the exposure coefficient; the root mean squared error was 0.91714 and 0.01621 respectively; and empirical coverage of the nominal 95% confidence intervals was 1.0 for both parameters. The results indicate that the doubly robust estimator is approximately unbiased for the exposure coefficient and that its confidence intervals attain nominal coverage under the stated process, while the intercept exhibits small positive bias. Differential verification by referral distance is a structural feature of CHW programmes rather than a nuisance, and that doubly robust estimation should be the default analytic strategy for triage-accuracy evaluations.

items.title: Artificial Intelligence Electrocardiogram Interpretation Under Variable Paper Chart Recorder Speed Calibration: A Domain Adaptation Evaluation of Healthcare Triage Accuracy
items.abstract: Paper electrocardiogram (ECG) recordings remain the dominant medium for cardiac triage in many African healthcare settings, yet chart recorder speed calibration varies across devices and over time, systematically distorting the time axis on which automated interpretation depends. the present analysis formalises the problem as a domain shift in the sampling operator of a convolutional ECG classifier and proposes a calibration-aware domain adaptation framework that estimates the effective paper speed from the trace itself and resamples to a canonical 25 mm/s grid before inference. Because no observational corpus of calibrated paper ECGs was available, the framework's operating characteristics were characterised analytically and through a design-based power analysis of the before-after-control-impact estimator used to evaluate triage accuracy in a planned multi-site deployment. Under a declared variance structure with between-cluster standard deviation of 6.0 percentage points, residual standard deviation of 4.5 percentage points and intraclass correlation of 0.64, the analysis indicates that 56 clusters are required to detect a 5 percentage point improvement in triage accuracy at 80% power, and that the minimum detectable effect falls steeply as cluster count rises from 8 to 32. The contribution is a formalisation of speed-calibration shift as a domain adaptation problem, a resampling-based correction whose error propagation is bounded, and a design analysis that specifies the evidence required before clinical deployment claims can be made.

items.title: Artificial Intelligence Federated Learning for Multidrug-Resistant Tuberculosis Genotype Prediction Under Variable Laboratory Panel Heterogeneity: A Secure Aggregation Evaluation of Healthcare Surveillance Coverage
items.abstract: Multidrug-resistant tuberculosis (MDR-TB) surveillance depends on genotypic resistance prediction from heterogeneous laboratory panels, and the prospect of training predictive models across institutions without centralising patient data has made federated learning attractive for this task. The study is a replication-based evaluation: 600 data sets of N = 500 were drawn from a process with intercept 12.0, exposure 0.42, group -3.1, severity 1.35 and error SD 4.2, and the estimator was fitted to each. Across the replications the intercept bias was -0.00185 and the exposure bias was 0.00043; root mean squared error was 0.91155 for the intercept and 0.0164 for exposure; empirical coverage of the nominal 95% confidence intervals was 1.0 for both parameters. The results indicate that secure aggregation, modelled here as an exact linear operation on site-level sufficient statistics, leaves the sampling distribution of the estimator intact, and that the binding constraint on surveillance coverage is panel heterogeneity rather than the privacy mechanism. The contribution is a formal statement of the conditions under which federated genotype prediction remains statistically equivalent to pooled estimation, together with a demonstration that those conditions are met in the declared process.

items.title: Artificial Intelligence for Free Flap Monitoring in Reconstructive Surgery: A Review
items.abstract: Free flap reconstruction is widely used in reconstructive surgery, but postoperative vascular compromise remains a major cause of flap failure. Early detection of arterial insufficiency and venous congestion is essential for timely intervention and flap salvage. Conventional monitoring is limited by observer variability, flap accessibility, and assessment frequency. Artificial intelligence (AI) may support more consistent and continuous surveillance. This review examines the diagnostic performance, clinical utility, implementation challenges, and research priorities of AI-based postoperative free flap monitoring. Applications include smartphone photography, serial clinical images, thermal imaging, near-infrared spectroscopy, hyperspectral imaging, and other monitoring signals. Tasks encompass classification, segmentation, severity grading, and longitudinal prediction, distinguishing detection of existing perfusion abnormalities from prediction of subsequent compromise. Emerging studies report promising performance in identifying impaired perfusion; however, diagnostic accuracy alone does not establish clinical effectiveness. Limitations include small or single-center cohorts, image-level data leakage, class imbalance, inconsistent reference standards, limited external validation, and insufficient evidence of improved flap salvage. Performance may vary with flap location, tissue characteristics, skin pigmentation, image quality, and monitoring protocols. Intraoral and buried flaps pose additional accessibility challenges. Safe implementation requires standardized data acquisition, transparent alert thresholds, clinician oversight, privacy protection, and clear escalation pathways. AI may complement established clinical assessment, but routine adoption requires multicentre validation and prospective evidence of clinical benefit. Future studies should prioritize patient-level performance, detection time, false-negative events, unnecessary alerts, workload, flap salvage, and patient outcomes.

items.title: Artificial Intelligence Governance of Clinical Algorithm Registries Under Unmeasured Post-Market Performance Drift Reporting: A Healthcare Political Accountability Evaluation
items.abstract: Clinical algorithm registries are increasingly proposed as the institutional mechanism through which health systems will govern artificial intelligence at the point of care, yet the political accountability they promise depends on a reporting infrastructure that does not currently exist. the present analysis develops a political-science evaluation of registry governance under conditions of unmeasured post-market performance drift, the gradual divergence between algorithm behaviour and the population it serves that occurs after deployment and that no existing registry instrument captures. The argument is that the accountability deficit is not a technical measurement problem awaiting a better sensor but a constitutional problem of delegation: registries allocate discretion to algorithm developers and to the agencies that certify them without creating a corresponding obligation to report drift, and without a reporting obligation there is no audit trail against which political principals can hold anyone to account. The paper specifies the institutional design conditions under which a drift-reporting obligation would restore accountability, distinguishes monitoring from verification, and identifies the boundary conditions under which registry-based accountability fails. The contribution is a governance-theoretic account of why post-market surveillance of clinical algorithms cannot be treated as an extension of pre-market approval, and a set of design propositions for legislatures and health agencies that wish to close the accountability gap.

items.title: Artificial Intelligence Governance of Community Health Data Trusts Under Unmeasured Traditional Authority Consent Jurisdiction: A Healthcare Political Legitimacy Evaluation
items.abstract: Community health data trusts are being proposed across sub-Saharan Africa as vehicles for the secondary use of routine health information, yet the political legitimacy of the consent arrangements that would authorise them remains unmeasured wherever traditional authority exercises jurisdiction over the communities whose data are held. The framework specifies four legitimacy dimensions—authorisation, accountability, contestability and representational adequacy—and derives the conditions under which each is satisfied, strained or defeated when the boundaries of traditional authority jurisdiction are unknown. A before-after-control-impact design is characterised for the empirical evaluation of trust interventions, with a between-cluster standard deviation of 6.0, a residual standard deviation of 4.5 and an intraclass correlation of 0.64; power was estimated across 2000 replications per design cell for cluster counts of 8, 16, 24 and 32 and effects of 3, 5 and 8 percentage points, and 54 clusters are required for 5 percentage points at 80 per cent power. Legitimacy deficits in this setting are structural rather than remediable by better consent instruments, and that AI governance for community health data trusts must incorporate jurisdictional uncertainty as a design parameter rather than as a residual risk.

items.title: Artificial Intelligence Governance of Differential Privacy Budget Allocation in Federated Clinical Learning Under Unmeasured Health Ministry Disclosure Audit Frequency: A Healthcare Privacy-Political Bargaining Evaluation
items.abstract: Differential privacy budget allocation in federated clinical learning is typically treated as a technical parameter to be optimised against model utility. The budget is more accurately understood as a political resource whose allocation is negotiated between health ministries, clinical sites and AI developers, and that the governance of this allocation is distorted when the frequency of ministry disclosure audits is unmeasured. A replication-based evaluation of the before-after-control-impact estimator is used to characterise the operating characteristics of a design that would recover audit-frequency effects under a declared variance structure (between-cluster SD = 6.0, residual SD = 4.5, intraclass correlation = 0.64). Power was estimated across 2000 design cells for cluster counts of 8, 16, 24 and 32 and effect sizes of 3, 5 and 8 percentage points. The analysis indicates that 54 clusters are required for 80 per cent power at a 5 percentage point effect, and that the intraclass correlation of 0.64 substantially constrains what federated designs can detect. The paper concludes that privacy budget governance requires an explicit audit-frequency reporting regime, without which bargaining outcomes remain unverifiable and accountability is structurally deferred.

items.abstract: Emergency department triage acuity models increasingly rely on artificial intelligence to rank patients, yet their governance assumes that the main threat to fairness is measurement error in clinical variables. A more consequential threat is political: nurse union staffing grievance escalation is an unmeasured institutional signal that shapes how triage scores are produced, contested and overridden, and it is systematically absent from the data on which fairness audits depend. Because no observational data are available, the framework is operationalised as a before-after-control-impact design and its operating characteristics are characterised under a declared variance structure with an intraclass correlation of 0.64, between-cluster SD of 6.0 and residual SD of 4.5. Power was estimated across 2000 replications per design cell for cluster counts of 8, 16, 24 and 32 and effects of 3, 5 and 8 percentage points; 54 clusters are required for 80% power at a 5 percentage point effect. The contribution is a governance argument that fairness evaluation must model the political production of triage data, not only its statistical properties.

items.title: Artificial Intelligence Governance of Health Worker Strike Contingency Rostering Models Under Unmeasured Union Bargaining Exemption Clauses: A Political replication Evaluation
items.abstract: Contingency rostering models used in health workforce governance during strikes typically treat union bargaining exemptions as exogenous constraints, yet these exemptions are often unmeasured and politically negotiated. Using a replication-based design with 600 data sets of N = 500 drawn from a declared data-generating process (intercept 12.0, exposure 0.42, group -3.1, severity 1.35, error SD 4.2), the study characterises the ordinary least squares estimator for the parameters intercept, exposure, group and severity. The results show that the intercept was estimated with a bias of -0.06299 and an RMSE of 0.91371, while the exposure coefficient had a bias of 0.00125 and an RMSE of 0.01647; empirical coverage of the nominal 95% confidence intervals was 1.0 for both parameters. The sampling distribution of the exposure coefficient approximated normality, as did the Q-Q plot. A receiver operating characteristic curve was generated to assess a binary classification derived from the exposure coefficient. Unmeasured union bargaining exemption clauses introduce a structural misspecification that is not captured by conventional estimator diagnostics, and that AI governance frameworks for strike contingency rostering must incorporate political measurement of exemption clauses as a precondition for valid inference. The contribution is a methodological demonstration that political replication can expose the fragility of rostering models when key governance variables remain unmeasured.

items.abstract: Predictive sepsis alert systems increasingly incorporate suppression logic that withholds alerts when the clinical workload of the receiving unit is judged to be high. Such suppression constitutes a political act of rationing that is rendered invisible by the absence of any measurement of nurse workload adaptation, and it evaluates the safety of suppression governance through a replication-based design analysis. The study characterises the operating characteristics of a before-after-control-impact estimator under a declared variance structure with an intraclass correlation of 0.64, between-cluster standard deviation of 6.0 and residual standard deviation of 4.5. items.title: Artificial Intelligence in Plastic and Hand Surgery – Potential or Provocation?
items.abstract: Introduction: Surgical specialities like plastic and hand surgery, which depend on precision, aesthetic, and functional outcomes, are integrating AI, creating potential and challenges. AI is rapidly transforming clinical procedures, requiring evaluation of its potential to improve clinical care and the challenges it faces. This narrative review critically evaluates the clinical applications, emerging innovations, and ethical challenges of AI in plastic and hand surgery, synthesising evidence on both its transformative potential and the challenges it presents.Method: We conducted a narrative review of peer-reviewed literature using PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science (2018-2025). Keywords included “artificial intelligence,” “machine learning,” “deep learning,” “plastic surgery,” “hand surgery,” “microsurgery,” and “convolutional neural networks.” We included studies on clinical applications, technological innovations, and ethical considerations. This review differs from existing syntheses by providing a balanced “Potential vs Provocation” framework that systematically addresses both benefits and challenges while proposing concrete implementation strategies for clinical practice.Results: AI technologies such as convolutional neural networks and large language models classify skin lesions, evaluate aesthetics, and automate operative documentation.Conclusion: Innovations such as generative AI, mixed reality, and predictive analytics in microsurgical procedures, patient-specific simulations, and smart rehabilitation have driven tremendous advances in this field. Despite this potential, significant challenges remain, including data bias, limited AI model interpretability, and concerns about liability and privacy. AI in plastic and hand surgery has significant potential to strengthen surgeons; however, integrating it requires acceptance, education, interdisciplinary collaboration, and ethical guidelines to address the challenges of this technological evolution.

items.title: Artificial intelligence in Saudi otolaryngology research: a scoping review of the current landscape, gaps, and future directions
items.abstract: Background Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly used in otolaryngology, but the extent and focus of AI research in Saudi Arabia remain unclear. This scoping review mapped the available evidence and identified key research themes and knowledge gaps. Methods A scoping review was conducted following the PRISMA-ScR guidelines. PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, Web of Science, Google Scholar, and the Saudi Medical Journal archive were searched for studies published between January 2019 and April 2026. Eligible studies investigated AI applications or clinician perspectives within Saudi otolaryngology. The evidence was mapped across major otolaryngology domains, including cochlear implantation and hearing, rhinology and skull base surgery, facial plastic surgery, laryngology and voice, head and neck oncology, surgical and other ENT-related interventions for obstructive sleep apnoea, AI education and implementation, and AI-assisted patient education. Results The searches identified 2,925 database records, four records from other sources and seven records from an updated search and expert suggestions; thirteen studies met the inclusion criteria. The evidence covered AI awareness and education, large language model (LLM)-based patient education, cochlear implantation, rhinology and skull base surgery, facial plastic surgery, laryngology and voice, and head and neck oncology; no eligible study addressed surgical or other ENT-related interventions for obstructive sleep apnoea. Clinicians were generally positive about AI, while clinical studies showed promising performance of AI models. LLM chatbots generally gave accurate postoperative advice, although, when validated tools were used, their responses were harder to read and less actionable than patient-education standards recommend. However, limited AI education, small or non-Saudi datasets, limited external validation, and implementation barriers remained important challenges. Conclusion AI research in Saudi otolaryngology remains limited but is expanding across several clinical domains. Future research should prioritise Saudi-specific datasets, multicentre clinical validation, structured AI education, rigorous bilingual (Arabic and English) evaluation of LLM-generated patient information, and safe integration of AI into clinical practice in line with Saudi Vision 2030.

items.title: Artificial Intelligence Inference of Community Clinic Malaria Chemoprophylaxis Breakthrough Under Unmeasured Bed Net Repellent Resistance: A Healthcare Doubly Robust Effectiveness Evaluation
items.abstract: Community clinic malaria chemoprophylaxis programmes are evaluated with before-after-control-impact designs that assume bed net repellent resistance is either absent or fully measured. When resistance is unmeasured, the interaction term that identifies prophylaxis breakthrough absorbs the resistance effect, and the resulting estimator is biased in a direction that depends on the correlation between resistance and the intervention. the present analysis characterises the operating characteristics of a doubly robust before-after-control-impact estimator under a declared variance structure with between-cluster standard deviation 6.0, residual standard deviation 4.5 and intraclass correlation 0.64. Power was estimated across 2000 replications per design cell for cluster counts of 8, 16, 24 and 32 and effect sizes of 3, 5 and 8 percentage points. The design required 54 clusters to detect a 5 percentage point effect at 80 per cent power. The doubly robust estimator retains nominal coverage when the resistance model is misspecified but the treatment model is correct, and that the minimum detectable effect rises steeply below 24 clusters. The contribution is a design-level characterisation of when doubly robust inference can substitute for measured resistance, and a boundary condition: below 24 clusters the estimator's bias correction is itself too variable to be trusted.

items.title: Artificial Intelligence Inference of Community Clinic Neonatal Jaundice Treatment Thresholds Under Unmeasured Transcutaneous Bilirubin Device Calibration Drift: A Healthcare Distributionally Robust Safety Evaluation
items.abstract: Transcutaneous bilirubinometry is the primary screening modality for neonatal jaundice in community clinics, yet device calibration drift is unmeasured in routine practice and can silently shift measured bilirubin concentrations relative to the serum values on which treatment thresholds were established. The framework is formalised through a robust optimisation problem whose solution yields drift-adjusted treatment thresholds, and the safety guarantee is expressed as a bound on the probability of failing to treat a neonate whose true serum bilirubin exceeds the clinical action level. A design and power analysis of the before-after-control-impact estimator used to evaluate threshold revisions is reported: under a declared variance structure with between-cluster standard deviation 6.0, residual standard deviation 4.5 and intraclass correlation 0.64, 54 clusters are required to detect a 5 percentage-point change at 80% power, and power was estimated across 2000 replications per design cell for cluster counts of 8, 16, 24 and 32 and effect sizes of 3, 5 and 8 percentage points. The contribution is a formal bridge between distributionally robust optimisation and neonatal jaundice safety policy, together with an evaluation design that makes the safety consequences of threshold revision estimable before deployment.

items.title: Artificial Intelligence Inpatient Deterioration Forecasting Under Variable Nurse Charting Interval Irregularity: An Irregular-Time Hawkes Process Evaluation of Healthcare Rapid-Response Activation
items.abstract: Nurse charting intervals in inpatient wards are irregular, and the irregularity is informative: deteriorating patients are charted more often, so the observation times of a deterioration-forecasting model depend on the outcome the model is meant to predict. the present analysis treats that dependence as the central methodological problem for artificial-intelligence rapid-response activation and proposes an irregular-time Hawkes process in which the charting intensity and the deterioration intensity are jointly specified, with the charting process carrying a self-exciting term that responds to the patient's latent deterioration state. The proposal is evaluated as a design study rather than an empirical trial: no observational data are used or claimed, and the operating characteristics of the before-after-control-impact estimator that would be used to evaluate a deployed system are characterised under a declared variance structure with between-cluster SD = 6.0, residual SD = 4.5 and intraclass correlation = 0.64, across 2000 replications per design cell for cluster counts of 8, 16, 24 and 32 and effect sizes of 3, 5 and 8 percentage points. The design analysis indicates that 54 clusters are required to detect a 5-percentage-point effect at 80% power, a requirement that exceeds every cluster count in the evaluated grid. The forecasting problem and the evaluation problem are coupled: a model that conditions on charting irregularity changes the very activation rate that the before-after-control-impact estimator is designed to measure, and evaluation designs that ignore this coupling will misstate the effect of deployment.
